blog.title: TrapLog: your wildlife control log, inspection-ready
blog.description: Log every control activity with the fields state inspectors ask for — species, method, disposition, client — then print a daily log or export a CSV for your annual report.

body.text: The log is the license. In several states, nuisance wildlife control operators must keep a daily record of every control activity — client, address, date, provider, species, number removed, method, disposition — current at the business location and ready for inspection. Paper notebooks fall behind, and a stale log at inspection time means violations, fines, and in Iowa, a blocked permit renewal. TrapLog exists so the record is never the thing that sinks you.

Log each control activity the day it happens, with the fields inspectors ask for. Species, control method, and disposition come as picklists built for wildlife work, so entries take seconds. Search and filter the log by date, client, or species, print an inspection-ready daily log, and export a CSV when annual-report time comes.

items: Pest companies with a wildlife division
